facts.statement: Cicimurri, Ebersole and Bowman are the authors who named Galeorhinus semiserratus.
Galeorhinus semiserratus lived during the Priabonian stage of the Eocene.
The type locality for Galeorhinus semiserratus is the Tupelo Bay Formation in South Carolina, United States.
facts.quote:
Type locality: Tupelo Bay Formation
Country: United States
Region: South Carolina

facts.statement: Galeorhinus semiserratus belongs to the genus Galeorhinus.
Galeorhinus semiserratus is classified in the family Triakidae.
The species is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
Fossils of Galeorhinus semiserratus are recorded from the Priabonian age, about 37.71 to 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Priabonian to Priabonian (37.71 to 33.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Galeorhinus semiserratus has been documented.

The description of Galeorhinus semiserratus appears in a 2026 paper titled "LATE EOCENE FISHES FROM THE TUPELO BAY FORMATION OF SOUTH CAROLINA, USA" published in Rivista Italiana di Paleontologia e Stratigrafia.

facts.statement: The authors of the study that named Galeorhinus semiserratus are David J. Cicimurri, Jun A. Ebersole, and Andrew R. Bowman.
facts.quote: Authors: DAVID J. CICIMURRI, JUN A. EBERSOLE, ANDREW R. BOWMAN

facts.statement: The Tupelo Bay Formation is an Eocene carbonate unit in the outer Atlantic Coastal Plain of South Carolina, USA.
Sharks of the order Carcharhiniformes are the most diverse in the Tupelo Bay Formation, with twelve taxa identified.
